prdTicketRef: SCH-010 (PRD header). The pipeline ticket is SH-10.

functionalRequirements.description: Add Prisma enums QuizStatus, QuestionType, ResultsVisibility, AttemptStatus and ScoringPolicy, and add the models Quiz, Question, QuizAttempt, QuizAnswer and QuizAccommodation exactly as listed in FR-1, in a new prisma migrate migration. Add the back-relations on Course and User.

Enforce the field limits from FR-1 in Zod validators (src/lib/validators/quiz.ts): availableUntil > availableFrom, timeLimitMinutes 1–300 or null, maxAttempts 1–10, points 0.5–100, extraTimeMinutes 0–300, extraAttempts 0–5, choice questions have 2–8 options, SHORT_ANSWER accepts 1–10 answers, ESSAY responses are at most 10,000 characters.
functionalRequirements.source: FR-1 field comments; FR-2 table; FR-3.1

functionalRequirements.description: Add pure auto-grading in src/server/quiz/grading.ts. SINGLE_CHOICE and TRUE_FALSE score all or nothing. MULTIPLE_CHOICE gives partial credit: points × max(0, (correctSelected − incorrectSelected) / totalCorrect). For the FR-2 example (4 points, correct {A,C}), {A,B} scores 0 and {A} scores 2.

SHORT_ANSWER grading trims the text and collapses whitespace, then matches it against any accepted answer. Matching ignores case unless caseSensitive is set. A non-match scores 0, is flagged for review, and a teacher can override it. ' Photosynthesis ' matches 'photosynthesis'.
ESSAY questions are never auto-graded. An optional guidance text is stored in `correct`.
Quiz builder page /courses/[courseId]/quizzes/[quizId]/edit. It has a settings panel for every Quiz field, with validation that the time limit is no longer than the availability window.

The builder question list supports add (type picker), inline edit, duplicate, delete and drag reorder (@dnd-kit with MUI items). Each type has its own editor: option rows with a correct radio or checkbox, an accepted-answers list, and essay guidance.
The builder shows a running points total. 'Preview as student' opens the player in a preview mode that records nothing.
Publishing requires at least 1 question, a correct answer on every choice question, and points > 0 on every question.

Once any attempt exists, only question text, explanation and accepted answers can be edited. Adding or removing questions and changing points or type are blocked with an explanation. A Regrade action (POST /api/quizzes/:id/regrade) recomputes auto-graded answers for all attempts.

Register a 'Quizzes' course tab in src/config/course-tabs.ts. Teachers see a list with status, window, attempt count, average score and 'Needs grading' count. Students see Upcoming, Available now (Start/Resume), Completed (score if visible) and Missed. Parents see completed results, read-only.

Quiz player start screen at /quizzes/[quizId]/take. It shows instructions, question count, total points, time limit and attempts used/allowed. 'Start attempt' asks for confirmation because the timer starts immediately.

Starting an attempt freezes questionOrder (shuffled when enabled) and the option order (deterministic shuffle seeded by attempt id). It sets deadlineAt = min(startedAt + timeLimit + extraTime, availableUntil).

Player layout uses MUI RadioGroup, FormGroup with Checkboxes or TextField per type, plus a LinearProgress for completion. It shows either all questions on one page or one per page with a navigator grid of MUI Buttons (answered, unanswered, flagged). A sticky header holds the title, an mm:ss timer that turns red under 2 minutes, and Submit.

Autosave sends PUT /api/attempts/:id/answers/:questionId, debounced 800 ms. Failed saves are queued in localStorage and retried every 5 s. A status pill shows 'All answers saved', 'Saving…' or 'Offline — answers saved on this device'.
The timer is display-only. The server rejects answer writes after deadlineAt + 30 s grace with 409 CONFLICT and auto-submits the attempt.

Submit asks for confirmation and shows the unanswered count. On submit, the attempt is auto-graded. Its status becomes NEEDS_GRADING if it has any ESSAY or any unmatched SHORT_ANSWER flagged for review; otherwise it becomes GRADED.

An IN_PROGRESS attempt past deadlineAt is auto-submitted with autoSubmitted = true. This happens lazily when the student or teacher loads it, and in autoSubmitExpiredAttempts() during the maintenance run.
Each student can have only one IN_PROGRESS attempt per quiz. Opening the quiz in a second tab, or reopening it, resumes the same attempt with its saved answers.

Results visibility: IMMEDIATELY shows results after submit, AFTER_CLOSE after availableUntil, and MANUAL after 'Release results' (POST /api/quizzes/:id/release-results sets resultsReleasedAt). Until then, students see 'Submitted — results will be available later.'
The result page shows the score, percentage, per-question correctness, the student's response and teacher feedback. It shows correct answers and explanations only when showCorrectAnswers is set.
Export getStudentQuizScore(quizId, studentId). It applies the scoring policy (HIGHEST, LATEST or AVERAGE) across GRADED attempts, for use by PRD-11.
The attempt limit is maxAttempts + extraAttempts. Further starts are refused. Example: with maxAttempts=2, a 3rd attempt is refused, but allowed with 1 extra attempt.

Manual grading page /courses/[courseId]/quizzes/[quizId]/grade. It has 'By student' and 'By question' modes, with points input (0 to question points, step 0.5) and feedback. Teachers can override auto-graded answers. Saving uses PUT /api/attempts/:id/answers/:questionId/grade.
When every answer in an attempt is graded, the attempt becomes GRADED and its score is recomputed.
The teacher Analytics tab shows attempts, average, median, highest, lowest, average time taken, and a score histogram (10% buckets, MUI X BarChart).

The analytics per-question table shows % correct and average points. For choice questions it also shows the option distribution, highlighting the most-chosen wrong option. GET /api/quizzes/:id/analytics?format=csv exports all attempts (student, attempt, score, per-question points).
Teachers grant extra time and extra attempts per student on the quiz settings page (PUT /api/quizzes/:id/accommodations/:studentId). Both values feed the deadlineAt and attempt-limit checks.
Register notification types quiz.published and quiz.results_released in src/server/notifications/types.ts. quiz.published goes to enrolled students on publish, with email off by default.

quiz.results_released goes to the student and their parents when results become visible. For AFTER_CLOSE it is sent once by the maintenance run after close; for MANUAL it is sent on release; for IMMEDIATELY nothing is sent.

Quiz and question CRUD REST endpoints follow the API table: GET/POST /api/courses/:id/quizzes (role-shaped list), GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/quizzes/:id (delete only without attempts), POST /api/quizzes/:id/questions, PATCH/DELETE /api/questions/:id, POST /api/quizzes/:id/questions/reorder.

Attempt endpoints: POST /api/quizzes/:id/attempts (STUDENT, start or resume), GET /api/attempts/:id (owner or manager), PUT /api/attempts/:id/answers/:questionId (owner), POST /api/attempts/:id/submit (owner).
Practice quizzes (isPractice=true) are ungraded and never reach the gradebook. getStudentQuizScore callers (PRD-11) must exclude them, so the service exposes the isPractice flag.

'manage' and 'view course' roles reuse the existing course-access checks in src/server/auth/course-access.ts: teacher of the course or ADMIN manage; enrolled students view; parents of enrolled students view read-only.
functionalRequirements.source: API table Role column; Platform Context: Roles; existing src/server/auth/course-access.ts

A dedicated student serializer enforces this, with a unit test asserting the `correct` key is absent. The GET /api/quizzes/:id student view never includes `correct`.

nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Reliability/performance: answer autosave handles 300 concurrent students saving every few seconds. Each save is one upsert on QuizAnswer (attemptId, questionId), under 50 ms.

Accessibility: the player is fully keyboard operable. Choice options are native radio/checkbox inputs (MUI Radio/Checkbox). Timer warnings use aria-live='assertive' and are announced at 5 and 1 minutes remaining.

UI component rule: Material UI only (@mui/material 9.5.0, icons, x-data-grid, x-date-pickers, x-charts). Every component is looked up through the mui-mcp server (useMuiDocs → fetchDocs) before use, and an unreachable MCP is a blocker. No banned libraries (Tailwind, shadcn, Radix, Recharts, notistack, etc.). Styling only via theme, sx and styled(). QA checks banned imports and that MUI imports resolve to documented components.

Server-side access control on every handler and server page via requireUser/requireRole/course access checks. Students can access only their own attempts, parents only their linked children's released results, and teachers only courses they teach.
nonFunctionalRequirements.source: Platform Context: Code layout (requireRole) and Roles

nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Tests: unit tests for every grading rule (partial credit, short-answer normalisation), deadline computation with accommodations, scoring policies, and the student serializer. Integration tests for autosave rejected after the deadline, auto-submit on load, and regrade. One Playwright e2e: teacher builds a 4-question quiz, student takes it with a mid-attempt reload, teacher grades the essay, student sees results. npm run lint && typecheck && test must stay green.
Usability goal: a teacher can build a 10-question multiple-choice quiz in under 10 minutes.
Out of scope: lockdown browser, webcam proctoring, shared or random question banks, LaTeX formula input.
